title: Development Setup
html:
Repository README · Validation · API runtime · Web workflow

This is the canonical local setup and execution path. Tests use disposable PostgreSQL and synthetic identities; no production database, identity provider, telemetry vendor, or deployment account is needed. Commands address workspace packages by path (pnpm -C apps/api …), so they work unchanged whatever a project names its packages.

Goal Prerequisites after installing pinned Node.js/pnpm Start here
Browse the documentation portal Frozen dependency install; no container, API, or test browser needed Portal
Run the API and web application locally Frozen dependency install, generated Prisma client, and local configuration Configuration
Use a local PostgreSQL or access-token issuer A database or issuer you control for development Local database and authentication
Run the complete validation gate All clean-checkout prerequisites, including containers and test browsers Prepare a clean checkout, then validate
Start a new project from Orion or upgrade a project's Orion baseline A fresh full clone and frozen dependency install Project derivation

Prepare a clean checkout

Use Node.js 24.13.0 and pnpm 11.25.0, as pinned by .node-version and package.json. For full validation, start Docker or another Testcontainers-compatible container runtime and verify that its daemon is reachable with docker info. From a fresh checkout, run:

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm db:generate
pnpm -C apps/web exec playwright install chromium

On Linux, use pnpm -C apps/web exec playwright install --with-deps chromium if the browser's system libraries are absent. Windows browser component tests use the installed Edge channel; Playwright end-to-end tests use Chromium. Media tests and the media module also need FFmpeg and ffprobe 6.1 or later on PATH (for example sudo apt-get install ffmpeg on Ubuntu 24.04, or winget install Gyan.FFmpeg on Windows); see ADR-0028. Do not put credentials in tracked files.

Load local configuration

For a new local configuration, copy the safe, schema-checked example into an ignored root .env.local file; preserve an existing file's settings. The example activates only ORION_ENV=development; uncomment and fill an optional setting only when needed. The API dev script uses Node's --env-file-if-exists to load this file before src/main.ts parses and validates configuration. Existing shell environment variables take precedence over file values. The following works in PowerShell and POSIX shells:

cp .env.example .env.local
pnpm -C apps/api dev

PowerShell also accepts Copy-Item .env.example .env.local. The default listener is 127.0.0.1:3000; GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/health/ready returns {"status":"ok"}. Without database or token settings, the API serves its health routes; modules that require the database or bearer authentication stay unmounted until those settings are configured. .env.local and other real environment files are ignored by Git; do not place secrets in .env.example.

Start the web development server in another terminal:

pnpm -C apps/web dev

Open the URL printed by Vite, normally http://127.0.0.1:5173. Vite forwards /api to the local API by default and loads its own apps/web/.env.local if web-specific VITE_ values are needed. Do not copy the root API .env.local into the web app: server-only values must not enter a browser build. Teluni's entry page sends visitors to sign-in and shows signed-in people their home page.

Local database and authentication

API configuration names the runtime settings. ORION_DATABASE_URL enables PostgreSQL for modules that require it and adds the database to readiness. The three token settings enable bearer authentication together; a trusted issuer must provide the claims described by the authentication policy.

For a separate local PostgreSQL, create distinct migration and restricted runtime credentials. Supply ORION_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL in the shell only for pnpm -C apps/api db:migrate:deploy; the Prisma CLI reads it from that process. Keep ORION_DATABASE_URL in the root ignored .env.local for the API runtime, alongside the trusted token issuer, audience and JWKS URL. Human sessions use the selected Keycloak realm and the additional identity settings in the configuration reference; the disposable identity stack is the available local qualification path. No persistent environment is provisioned by this guide. Do not copy Testcontainers' synthetic credentials into a persistent environment, and clear the migration credential from the shell after deployment.

Living Documentation Portal

The portal needs no API, database, identity provider, or .env.local. After the clean-checkout install above, run pnpm -C apps/web dev and open http://127.0.0.1:5173/docs (or the Vite-printed port plus /docs). Use its section navigation and breadcrumbs for API operations, tables, component examples, architecture, guides, policies, and ADRs. Repository documentation opens locally with headings and search, rather than requiring GitHub. Relevant sections also expose AI-readable OpenAPI, database, error, and component references.

To try an API route, also run the API as described above, open an API operation, enter declared inputs and a token when the operation requires one, then select Send request. Writes require explicit acknowledgement. Tokens and responses remain in memory; no request executes automatically. Cancellation/timeouts do not prove a write was undone. Without the API, reading remains available and request failures are shown safely.

After editing repository Markdown or reference sources, run pnpm docs:references:write and pnpm docs:references:check. A normal pnpm -C apps/web build excludes the internal portal and all of its generated assets. For an explicitly authorized internal artifact or local production-preview check, use PowerShell process environment variables:

$env:ORION_WEB_DOCUMENTATION = 'internal'
$env:ORION_WEB_INTERNAL_DOCS_ACCESS = 'external'
try { pnpm -C apps/web build } finally {
  Remove-Item Env:ORION_WEB_DOCUMENTATION
  Remove-Item Env:ORION_WEB_INTERNAL_DOCS_ACCESS
}
pnpm -C apps/web exec vite preview --host 127.0.0.1

Open /docs on the printed loopback port. The access setting acknowledges external enforcement; it does not install or verify it. Before any internal deployment, follow the full-artifact access policy. Preview always serves the already-built artifact. Rebuild without those variables before product distribution. Internal static serving needs the SPA fallback for nested routes plus protection for every asset; no deployment provider is selected here.

Persistent local environment

For day-to-day development with data that survives restarts, start the local services once and run the API and web application in watch mode. With Docker running, from the repository root:

pnpm db:generate
pnpm -C apps/api dev:services up
pnpm -C apps/api dev
pnpm -C apps/web dev

dev:services up creates or starts named containers (PostgreSQL on 127.0.0.1:55433, Keycloak on localhost:8180 with its management port on 9180, Mailpit with SMTP on 127.0.0.1:1025 and its inbox on http://127.0.0.1:8025) with named volumes, applies the committed migrations and runtime grants, provisions the teluni realm with the Teluni sign-in theme, creates the synthetic developer account dev@teluni.test, creates the ignored .dev-media/ media volume, and writes the root .env.local the API loads (the media module also needs FFmpeg on PATH). Machine-local credentials (database, Keycloak bootstrap administrator, client secrets, key rings and the developer password) are generated once and kept in the ignored .env.dev-services; a previous .env.local is copied to .env.local.before-dev-services. Open http://127.0.0.1:5173; invitation and verification emails arrive in the Mailpit inbox. Rerun up after pulling new migrations or realm changes. pnpm -C apps/api dev:services down stops the containers and keeps their data; reset removes containers, volumes, network and .dev-media/ so the next up starts empty. Keycloak's back-channel logout cannot reach an API listening on loopback, so in this environment provider-side sign-outs end panel sessions through the 30-second revalidation instead. These are development services only; never point the script or its credentials at shared or production systems.

Two-step verification

Two-step verification is optional for each person. Sign in with the password alone, or enable an authenticator app from the Sessões page (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or any TOTP app); from then on Keycloak asks for its code at every sign-in. Disabling it asks for the password and the current code. A new account is offered it right after its first sign-in. The former TELUNI_DEV_MFA_MODE setting no longer exists; remove it from .env.local if present (it is ignored). See the identity design.

Try sign-in locally

The identity workflow needs a Keycloak that the API calls back, so it runs as a disposable stack rather than with .env.local. With Docker running, from the repository root:

pnpm db:generate
pnpm -C apps/api build
node apps/web/test/e2e/identity/manual.ts

It starts a migrated PostgreSQL with the restricted runtime role, the pinned Keycloak with the provisioned teluni realm and one synthetic verified user, Mailpit as the mail inbox, the emitted API with generated session keys and client secrets, and Vite. It also configures the API's mail relay to Mailpit. It prints the panel URL, the Mailpit inbox URL and the email and password of a synthetic user and of a synthetic invitee; invitations sent from a company's Invitations view arrive in Mailpit, and you can also create an account on the Keycloak sign-in page and read its verification email there. Every credential is generated for that run only, and Ctrl+C discards all containers and data. The same stack drives the identity browser journeys.

Exercise automated workflows

Automated workflows use disposable databases and synthetic identities. No seed data or external account is needed:

pnpm build
pnpm smoke
pnpm test:e2e

pnpm smoke exercises the emitted API process, then any module process smokes. pnpm test:e2e runs the emitted API and the Vite web app for the shared documentation and shell journeys; module journeys start their own migrated PostgreSQL and synthetic issuer through the shared end-to-end stack helpers. These fixtures are disposable and are not release or production data.

Validate, regenerate, and build

Run the full, non-mutating tracked-source gate after changes:

pnpm validate

It checks format, lint, types, dependency boundaries, documentation, .env.example against API configuration metadata, migration release history, project provenance, current generated references, real PostgreSQL and browser tests, builds, and process smokes. pnpm references:check diagnoses generated API/database/SDK drift independently; it migrates a fresh PostgreSQL for the physical database reference and does not repair tracked files. To intentionally change those references, edit their canonical TypeBox/schema/metadata sources and run pnpm -C apps/api references:write, then pnpm -C packages/sdk generate after an OpenAPI change. Review the generated diff and rerun pnpm references:check.

After intentional repository Markdown, API, database, or component-metadata changes, run pnpm docs:references:write and review the generated component Markdown, catalog, detail pages, and search shards. Vite serves/emits the existing API, database, error, and component artifacts without committing duplicate copies. pnpm docs:references:check is non-mutating and fails on drift, missing component metadata, or known secret patterns; it runs within pnpm validate and CI. Do not edit either generated layer directly.

pnpm build emits the API ESM and web static assets into ignored dist/ directories and checks the browser bundle for known server-only markers. The release evolution workflow governs migrations; no durable release is recorded merely by running these commands.
